name: Sikadur-33
paste:
SIKADUR®-33: SPECIFICATION CLAUSE SET

Source: Sikadur®-33, April 2023, Version 01.04 (https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/d/sikadur_-33.pdf)
Draft for specifier review. Wording, values and standards are quoted from that data sheet; where it is silent the clause says 'Refer to manufacturer.' Confirm the current edition before issue.

1 SCOPE
1.1 Work included. Provide Sikadur®-33 where documented, installed or applied in accordance with this clause and the manufacturer's Product Data Sheet (April 2023, Version 01.04).
1.2 Product description. Sikadur-33 is a 2-component, 100% solids, moisture-tolerant, high-modulus, high-strength, structural, smooth-paste epoxy adhesive.
1.3 Intended uses stated by the manufacturer - As a structural adhesive for.
    - Concrete elements
    - Hard natural stone
    - Ceramics, fibre cement
    - Mortar, Bricks, Blocks, Masonry, render etc.
    - Steel, Iron, Aluminium
    - Wood
    - Polyester, Epoxy
    - Corners and edges
    - Hole and void filling
    - Joint arrises
    For concrete repairs
    Interior, vertical and overhead repair of:
1.4 Intended uses stated by the manufacturer - Joint filling and crack sealing.
    - Crack filling and sealing (non-moving)
1.5 Intended uses stated by the manufacturer - Metalwork, carpentry.
    - Fixing and fastening of handrails, railings, balustrades and supports
    - Fixing of window and door frames
1.6 Intended uses stated by the manufacturer - For use in the following.
    - Concrete
    - Hard natural stone
    - Solid rock
    - Hollow and solid masonry
    - Steel
    - Wood
1.7 Limits of use. Observe the manufacturer's limitations stated in clause 4.8.

2 MATERIALS
2.1 Product. Sikadur®-33
    - Product type as printed on the data sheet: High Modulus, High-Strength, Structural, Rapid Curing Epoxy, Smooth-Paste Adhesive
    - Supplier as printed on the data sheet: Sika Australia Pty Limited, ABN 12 001 342 329, aus.sika.com, Tel: 1300 22 33 48
2.2 Approvals / certificates.
    - Adhesive for structural bonding tested according to EN 1504-4, provided with the CE-mark
    - Potable Water approved to AS4020:2018 - Testing of products for use in contact with drinking water.
    - Qld Roads (TMR) Section 5. Registered and Conforming Products. Part 5.18 Epoxy paste for Bearing Installation
2.3 Standards and test methods cited in the data sheet. Cited as written in the data sheet. A citation is not a statement that the product complies with it; conformity is stated only where the data sheet says so (see the approvals clause and the statements quoted in the other clauses).
    - EN 1504-4: listed under approvals, certificates or standards. Where: Approvals / Certificates (p.1).
    - AS4020:2018: listed under approvals, certificates or standards. Where: Approvals / Certificates (p.1).
    - AS 1478.2: test method printed beside a stated value. Where: Technical Information > Compressive strength (p.2).
    - EN 12190: test method printed beside a stated value. Where: Technical Information > Compressive strength (p.2).
    - EN 196: test method printed beside a stated value. Where: Technical Information > Tensile strength in flexure (p.2).
    - DIN EN ISO 527-3: test method printed beside a stated value. Where: Technical Information > Tensile strength (p.2).
    - EN 1542: test method printed beside a stated value. Where: Technical Information > Tensile adhesion strength (p.2).
    - EN 4624: test method printed beside a stated value. Where: Technical Information > Tensile adhesion strength (p.2).
    - EN 1770: test method printed beside a stated value. Where: Technical Information > Coefficient of thermal expansion (p.2).
    - EN 12614: test method printed beside a stated value. Where: Technical Information > Glass transition temperature (p.2).
2.4 Characteristics stated by the manufacturer.
    - Can be used on damp concrete
    - Excellent adhesion to the substrate
    - Non-sag, also overhead
    - High load capacity
    - Shrinkage-free hardening
    - Styrene-free
2.5 Composition, appearance and supply.
    - Composition: Epoxy resin
    - Colour: Component A: white; Component B: grey; Components A + B mixed: Concrete grey
    - Density: 1.35 kg/l (component A+B mixed) (at +23 °C)
2.6 Properties stated by the manufacturer.
    - Shrinkage: Hardens without shrinkage
    - Coefficient of thermal expansion: 9.3 x 10⁻⁵ per °C (Temp. range +23 °C − +60 °C) (EN 1770)
    - Glass transition temperature: +49°C (7 days / +23°C) (EN 12614)
2.7 Compressive strength.
    | Curing time | Curing temperature |
    | +23 °C |
    | 1 day | ~30 N/mm² |
    | 7 days | ~40 N/mm² |
    | 14 days | ~43 N/mm² |
    | 14 days | ~50 N/mm² |
    (Table as printed; a cell that wraps appears over several rows.)
    Test method printed: (AS 1478.2)
    Test method printed: (EN 12190)
2.8 Tensile strength in flexure.
    | Curing time | Curing temperature |
    | +23 °C |
    | 14 days | ~20 N/mm² |
    (Table as printed; a cell that wraps appears over several rows.)
    Test method printed: (EN 196)
2.9 Tensile strength.
    | Curing time | Curing temperature |
    | +23 °C |
    | 14 days | ~13 N/mm² |
    (Table as printed; a cell that wraps appears over several rows.)
    Test method printed: (DIN EN ISO 527-3)
2.10 Tensile adhesion strength.
    | Curing time | Substrate | Adhesion |
    | strength |
    | 3 days | Dry concrete | >5 N/mm²* |
    | 3 days | Dry concrete | >5 N/mm²* |
    | 3 days | Blastcleaned steel | >10 N/mm² |
    | 3 days | Dry brick | >1.5 N/mm²** |
    (Table as printed; a cell that wraps appears over several rows.)
    Test method printed: (EN 1542 / EN 4624)
    Note printed: *100% concrete failure **100% brick failure
2.11 Packaging, shelf life and storage.
    - Packaging: 2.7 kg kit (2 litres); 27 kg kit (20 litres)
    - Shelf life: 12 months from date of production
    - Storage conditions: Store in original, unopened, sealed and undamaged packaging in dry conditions at temperatures between +10 °C and +30 °C. Protect from direct sunlight.

3 SUBSTRATE PREPARATION
3.1 General. Prepare substrates in accordance with the manufacturer's Product Data Sheet (April 2023, Version 01.04) and the requirements below. Inspect the substrate against these requirements before application.
3.2 Substrate quality. Mortar and concrete must be older than 28 days. Adequate substrate strength (concrete, masonry, natural stone) must always be confirmed.

4 APPLICATION
4.1 General. Apply in accordance with the manufacturer's Product Data Sheet (April 2023, Version 01.04) and the requirements below.
4.2 Application data.
    - Mixing ratio: Component A : component B = 1 : 1 by volume
    - Consumption: ~1.35 kg/m2 per mm of thickness. This figure is theoretical and does not allow for any additional material due to surface porosity, surface profile, variations in level or wastage etc.
    - Layer thickness: 0.5 mm min. / 10 mm max.
    - Sag flow: Non-sag, suitable for overhead applicaiton
    - Pot Life: 60 minutes (+23°C)
4.3 Open Time.
    | Temperature | Open Time Tgel |
    | +10 °C | 210 minutes |
    | +20 °C | 90 minutes |
    | +35 °C | 45 minutes |
    Note printed: Minimum cartridge temperature +10 °C
4.4 Curing time.
    | Temperature | Curing Time Tcur |
    | +10 °C | 3 days* |
    | +20 °C | 2 days* |
    | +35 °C | 1 day* |
    Note printed: *To achieve approx. 80% of the performance Minimum cartridge temperature +10 °C
4.5 Mixing. Pre-mix each component. Proportion equal parts by volume of Component „B‟ and Component „A‟ into a clean pail. Mix thoroughly for 3 minutes with Sika paddle on low speed (400-600 rpm) drill until uniform in colour. Mix only the quantity that can be used within its potlife.
4.6 Application method / tools.
    - Apply Sikadur-33 to the prepared substrate by trowel or gloved hand. Ensure the material is worked well (scrubbed) into the surface, this is particularly important on damp surfaces. There should be no standing water on concrete surfaces.
    - If using Sikadur-33 as an adhesive, coat both adherents and press into place (on vertical and overhead surfaces temporary support must be provided). The adhesive layer should not be less than 2 mm.
    - To seal injection ports and crack for injection grouting – Place the neat mixed material over the cracks to be pressure-injected and around each injection port. Allow sufficient time to set before pressure-injecting. Use Sikadur-52 for the low-viscosity injection adhesive. Consult the Technical Data Sheet on this product for more information. Also contact Technical Services for additional information on pressure-injection grouting.
    - To anchor bolts, dowels, pins – Annular space around bolt should not exceed 3 mm, depth of embedment is typically 10-15 times the bolt diameter. Grout with neat Sikadur-33.
4.7 Cleaning of equipment. Uncured material may be cleaned from application tools, etc. by using Sika Colma Cleaner (flammable solvent). Cured material can only be removed mechanically.
4.8 Limitations and important considerations.
    - Minimum substrate and ambient temperature 4ºC.
    - Do not thin. Addition of solvents will prevent proper cure.
    - Material is a vapour barrier after cure.
    - Not for sealing and cracks under hydrostatic pressure at the time of application.

5 QUALITY CONTROL AND TESTING
5.1 Hold point. Before each application, measure and record the conditions in clause 5.2 and compare them with the manufacturer's limits. HOLD POINT: do not proceed until the Superintendent has released the hold point.
5.2 Ambient air temperature. +10 °C min. / +35 °C max.
5.3 Relative air humidity. 85% max. (at 25 °C)
5.4 Dew point. Beware of condensation. Substrate temperature during application must be at least 3 °C above dew point.
5.5 Substrate temperature. +10 °C min. / +35 °C max.
5.6 Substrate moisture content. Substrate must be dry or mat damp (no standing water)
5.7 Conditions stated in the limitations. Also stated in the data sheet limitations (clause 4.8):
    - Minimum substrate and ambient temperature 4ºC.
5.8 Test methods printed beside stated values. Each value is as printed in the data sheet with its test method.
    - Compressive strength: Curing time | Curing temperature; +23 °C; 1 day | ~30 N/mm²; 7 days | ~40 N/mm²; 14 days | ~43 N/mm²; 14 days | ~50 N/mm² (AS 1478.2) (EN 12190)
    - Tensile strength in flexure: Curing time | Curing temperature; +23 °C; 14 days | ~20 N/mm² (EN 196)
    - Tensile strength: Curing time | Curing temperature; +23 °C; 14 days | ~13 N/mm² (DIN EN ISO 527-3)
    - Tensile adhesion strength: Curing time | Substrate | Adhesion; strength; 3 days | Dry concrete | >5 N/mm²*; 3 days | Dry concrete | >5 N/mm²*; 3 days | Blastcleaned steel | >10 N/mm²; 3 days | Dry brick | >1.5 N/mm²** (EN 1542 / EN 4624)
    - Coefficient of thermal expansion: 9.3 x 10⁻⁵ per °C (Temp. range +23 °C − +60 °C) (EN 1770)
    - Glass transition temperature: +49°C (7 days / +23°C) (EN 12614)
5.9 Basis of the stated values. All technical data stated in this Product Data Sheet are based on laboratory tests. Actual measured data may vary due to circumstances beyond our control.
5.10 Other tests. For any test method, sampling frequency or acceptance criterion not stated in this clause: refer to manufacturer and the project specification.

6 WARRANTY AND DOCUMENTATION
6.1 Documents to be obtained and submitted. Obtain the current issue of each document before ordering and submit it with the product submission. Documents are listed as published on the manufacturer's website.
    - Product Data Sheet: Sikadur®-33, April 2023, Version 01.04, https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/d/sikadur_-33.pdf
    - Safety Data Sheet: SDS Sikadur®-33 Part A, version 10/12/2025, https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/i/sds-sikadur-33-parta.pdf
6.2 Ecology, health and safety. For information and advice on the safe handling, storage and disposal of chemical products, users shall refer to the most recent Safety Data Sheet (SDS) containing physical, ecological, toxicological and other safety-related data.
6.3 Warranty. Obtain any product or installation warranty in writing from the manufacturer or its authorised applicator and file it with the project records. Warranty terms: refer to manufacturer.
    - Legal notes: In practice, the differences in materials, substrates and actual site conditions are such that no warranty in respect of merchantability or of fitness for a particular purpose, nor any liability arising out of any legal relationship whatsoever, can be inferred either from this information, or from any written recommendations, or from any other advice offered.
6.4 Local restrictions. Please note that as a result of specific local regulations the declared data for this product may vary from country to country. Please consult the local Product Data Sheet for the exact product data.
6.5 Application records. Record the product name, batch numbers, dates, areas treated and the conditions measured under clause 5.2, and include the records in the project documentation.
